headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line while funding stays positive and whales park coin on exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it answers the only question that matters before you look at anything else: none of the seven majors here are above their 200-day moving average. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, all below, all lacking a golden cross. That is a uniform picture, not a mixed one, and it tells you the broader trend structure is still down or at best unsettled across the board, even though BTC is still up 5.52% over 30 days and ADA is up 18.05% over the same window. Bounces inside a downtrend are still bounces.

Momentum is where the story gets more interesting, because it does not agree cleanly with that trend picture. RSI readings are mostly in neutral territory, not oversold: BTC at 44.6, ETH at 51.5, SOL at 53.6, BNB at 62.4. XRP is the outlier at 36.7, closer to weak. MACD is split down the middle, above signal for SOL, BNB, and DOGE, below for BTC, ETH, XRP, ADA. That split, combined with sub-200-day prices, reads as a market resting rather than accelerating in either direction. Nobody's momentum is screaming, which matches a Fear & Greed reading of 29, sitting mid-range against its own 30-day band of 25 to 33.

Positioning adds a wrinkle worth naming plainly. Funding on OKX is positive across the board, meaning longs are paying shorts to hold their bets: BTC at an annualized 10.1%, ETH at 11.0%, DOGE also at 11.0%, XRP at 8.9%. The long/short account ratio confirms crowds are leaning long everywhere, from BTC's 1.87 up to DOGE's lopsided 5.29. That is a market with a lot of bullish conviction paying a toll to stay positioned that way, and the 24-hour liquidation tape shows who has been getting hurt for it: BTC longs lost $6.0M against $2.1M for shorts, ETH longs lost $10.3M against $2.6M for shorts. Crowded and paying up is a fragile combination, not because it forecasts a direction, but because it means one side has more capital exposed to a move against it.

The flow data leans the same way as the liquidations. Whale wallets moved a net $262.8M onto exchanges over the last 48 hours, with BTC specifically seeing $385.1M in and $122.3M out. The single biggest move was $216.6M in USDT into OKX, alongside BTC deposits of $127.5M into Coinbase Institutional and $117.4M into Binance. Coin and stablecoin landing on exchanges is usually read as dry powder being staged for a decision, either to sell or to buy, and the four-session weekly trend behind it has been genuinely choppy: -$335.9M, then +$1,382.1M, then +$812.0M, then -$761.3M. No persistent direction there, just volatility in the flow itself. On the ETF side, BTC funds saw -$61.1M on 12 Aug but the last five sessions net positive at +$41.4M, same_direction_days of only 1, so treat that single day as a data point, not a trend. ETH ETFs took in +$7.4M on the same day with a stronger five-session net of +$132.8M, again only one same-direction day behind it. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is essentially flat, down just 0.58% over 30 days to $306.4B, so the fuel tank isn't visibly draining.

Put the sentiment gauge next to all of this and the disagreement is mild rather than dramatic. Fear & Greed at 29 says the crowd feels cautious, but positioning (long-heavy, funding-positive) says traders are still betting on upside, and BTC's own price is roughly flat on the day at -0.21% and up over the trailing month. The crowd's mood and the crowd's money are not quite telling the same story, which is itself the more interesting read than either number alone.

What's worth watching from here: whether funding stays positive while OI holds near $2.06B on BTC and $1.34B on ETH (a crowded long book that keeps paying up is a different risk than one that unwinds), whether the ETF five-session trend on BTC turns into more than one same-direction day, and whether the whale exchange-inflow pattern extends into a longer stretch instead of reversing like it has three times in the last four windows. A reclaim of the 200-day average on any major, none have one now, would also be a structural change worth noting rather than assuming.
